about: What an engine or stack leaves behind in a shipped game or app: install layout, file formats, scripting, which ReversePort tools read it, and the natural rebuild target. Used by re_lookup (to tell an agent where the material is and how it is structured, without files) and re_blueprint. Only layouts that are stable across versions are listed.

unity.name: Unity
layout: <Game>.exe + UnityPlayer.dll (Windows player)
<Game>_Data/ — globalgamemanagers (holds the Unity version), level0…levelN (scenes), sharedassets*.assets, resources.assets
<Game>_Data/Managed/Assembly-CSharp.dll — game code (Mono builds)
GameAssembly.dll + <Game>_Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata/global-metadata.dat — game code compiled to native (IL2CPP builds)
<Game>_Data/StreamingAssets/ — files shipped as-is (often AssetBundles, videos, configs)
readWith: re_scan on the install folder → engine, version, Mono or IL2CPP
re_binary on Assembly-CSharp.dll → classes and methods (Mono)
unity.limits: IL2CPP builds have no .NET assemblies: only native code plus metadata. Asset files are binary serialized; ReversePort lists and probes them but does not unpack them.

godot.name: Godot
layout: <Game>.exe / .x86_64 + <Game>.pck (or the pack embedded at the end of the executable)
inside the pack: project.godot, *.tscn/*.scn scenes, *.gd scripts (text or tokenized), .import/ converted assets
C# games: data_<Game>_<platform>/ with the .NET assemblies
readWith: re_archive on the .pck or .exe → list/extract scenes and scripts
godot.limits: Encrypted packs are reported and left alone.

unreal.name: Unreal Engine
layout: <Project>/Binaries/<Platform>/<Project>-<Platform>-Shipping.exe — game code (native)
<Project>/Content/Paks/*.pak — cooked assets (UE5 also .utoc/.ucas IoStore containers)
Engine/ — engine binaries and shared content
readWith: re_binary on the Shipping exe → imports, sections, strings
unreal.limits: Paks are often encrypted and cooked assets are binary; no source code ships. Rebuild from observation.

gamemaker.name: GameMaker
layout: <Game>.exe + data.win (all rooms, sprites, sounds and compiled code in one file); YYC builds compile GML to native code
readWith: re_probe on data.win → chunk layout, embedded PNG/OGG
gamemaker.limits: YYC builds contain native code only.

rpgmaker.name: RPG Maker MV/MZ
layout: www/ or root: index.html, js/rpg_*.js (MV) or js/rmmz_*.js (MZ), js/plugins/*.js, data/*.json (maps, actors, items, events), img/, audio/

renpy.name: Ren'Py
layout: game/ with *.rpy (source), *.rpyc (compiled), *.rpa (archives with images/audio)
renpy/ engine, lib/ Python runtime

love2d.name: LÖVE
layout: <Game>.exe with a .love (zip) appended, or a .love file next to love.exe; main.lua + conf.lua inside
readWith: re_probe on the exe → embedded ZIP offset

source.name: Source engine (Valve)
layout: <game>/ with gameinfo.txt, bin/ (client.dll, server.dll), *.vpk archives, maps/*.bsp (Source 2: .vpk with .vmap_c)

electron.name: Electron
layout: <App>.exe + resources/app.asar (the app's JS/HTML/CSS) or resources/app/ unpacked; *.node native modules

nwjs.name: NW.js
layout: nw.exe/<Game>.exe + package.nw (zip) or package.json + html/js next to it (Construct 2/3 and RPG Maker MV desktop exports use it)
readWith: re_probe on the exe for an appended zip

monogame.name: MonoGame / XNA / FNA
layout: <Game>.exe/.dll (.NET) + Content/*.xnb (compiled content)
readWith: re_binary on the game .exe/.dll → .NET types and methods

construct.name: Construct
layout: HTML5 export: index.html, scripts/c3runtime.js (Construct 3) or c2runtime.js, data.json (project data), images/, media/

defold.name: Defold
layout: game.arcd + game.arci (resource archive and index), game.dmanifest, game.projectc

cocos.name: Cocos2d-x / Cocos Creator
layout: Android: lib/<abi>/libcocos2d*.so or libcocos*.so, assets/ with .jsc/.luac or res/ and src/

libgdx.name: libGDX / Java
layout: desktop: <game>.jar (classes + assets); Android: classes*.dex + assets/

flutter.name: Flutter
layout: Android: lib/<abi>/libapp.so (compiled Dart) + libflutter.so, assets/flutter_assets/ (images, fonts, AssetManifest)
iOS: Frameworks/App.framework + flutter_assets

react-native.name: React Native
layout: Android: assets/index.android.bundle (JS or Hermes bytecode); iOS: main.jsbundle

web.name: Web app / browser game
layout: index.html + bundled scripts (often hashed names under /assets or /_next), styles, images, .wasm and data files loaded at runtime
readWith: re_lookup {url} lists the scripts, wasm and data files the page loads
